Vendored third-party code for the GeneralsX native renderer (GXRender). Approved by the lead (C31, 10/10/2026): pinned
release tags from the official repositories, LICENSE files kept, no network fetch at build time. Both are MIT, which is
GPL-3.0-compatible. Files are byte-identical copies of the release archives; never edit them here - re-vendor instead.

volk - Vulkan meta-loader
  repo     https://github.com/zeux/volk
  tag      vulkan-sdk-1.4.357.0  (commit 776893306c5d3b22b6185b5d4a258b81d94572bf, 2026-07-18)
  archive  https://github.com/zeux/volk/archive/refs/tags/vulkan-sdk-1.4.357.0.tar.gz
           sha256 6400c7b23e24d17e4f04bac49b55b06c4e87677d33398e90344743ec73560ca6
  files    volk/volk.c      sha256 e3401bab5e1d69b4e09fb95143490cda40740a3d3906c4e99f388071c7809602
           volk/volk.h      sha256 036348b6f0dd7310c5e3bc04417be9ee56271c9997bd5eca49946ed52eca0e76
           volk/LICENSE.md  sha256 04a0693a84f19e53d281ca98bbb0c86ca77251ab13769c6168e6684feb9a1436
  note     VkCtx never calls volkInitialize(): it resolves vkGetInstanceProcAddr itself (the caller's - SDL3's in the game -
           or the DXVK fork's per-platform search list) and hands it to volkInitializeCustom(), so the renderer and the
           window surface always come from the same Vulkan library.

Checks done before vendoring (E · rw1-B, 10/10/2026): licences read (MIT, both); the sources grepped for process/network
calls (system/popen/exec/socket/connect/curl/fork: none; volk's only dynamic loading is its own volkInitialize search list,
which VkCtx does not call). The exposure-scan skill could not run on this MacBook (bumblebee/Go not installed) and its
catalogs cover package ecosystems (npm/PyPI/Go/gems/extensions), not vendored C sources.
